title.en: Clone a list with jump links
title.es: Clonar una lista con enlaces de salto

prompt.en:
Each node of a singly linked list has `val`, `next` and `jump`, where `jump` points at any node of the same list (itself included) or is `None`. Write `clone(head)`: return the first node of a deep copy, made of new nodes with the same values, whose `next` and `jump` point at the copy's own nodes in the same positions. Values can repeat. Leave the original list as you found it.

Aim for O(n) time; O(1) extra memory besides the copy is possible.

The tests call the provided `run_clone(values, jumps)`: `jumps[i]` is the index of the node that node `i` jumps to, or `null` for none. It returns your copy's values and, for each copy node, the index its jump points at.
prompt.es:
Cada nodo de una lista enlazada simple tiene `val`, `next` y `jump`, donde `jump` apunta a cualquier nodo de la misma lista (incluido él mismo) o es `None`. Escribe `clone(head)`: devuelve el primer nodo de una copia profunda, hecha de nodos nuevos con los mismos valores, cuyos `next` y `jump` apuntan a los propios nodos de la copia en las mismas posiciones. Los valores pueden repetirse. Deja la lista original tal como la encontraste.

Apunta a O(n) en tiempo; se puede con O(1) de memoria extra, sin contar la copia.

Los tests llaman a `run_clone(values, jumps)`, ya incluida: `jumps[i]` es el índice del nodo al que salta el nodo `i`, o `null` si no salta. Devuelve los valores de tu copia y, para cada nodo de la copia, el índice al que apunta su salto.

hints.en: Make the copies first, then wire them: a dictionary from each original node to its copy turns every `jump` into one lookup. Key it by node, not by value: values repeat.
hints.es: Primero crea las copias y después conéctalas: un diccionario de cada nodo original a su copia convierte cada `jump` en una sola búsqueda. Usa el nodo como clave, no el valor: los valores se repiten.

hints.en: For O(1) extra memory, put each copy right after its original (`A → A' → B → B'`). Then the copy of `node.jump` is simply `node.jump.next`.
hints.es: Para O(1) de memoria extra, pon cada copia justo después de su original (`A → A' → B → B'`). Así, la copia de `node.jump` es simplemente `node.jump.next`.

hints.en: Finish by unzipping the two lists: each original takes back its old `next`, and the copies link to each other. The original must end up intact.
hints.es: Termina separando las dos listas: cada original recupera su `next` de antes y las copias se enlazan entre sí. El original debe quedar intacto.

solution:
# --- your code ---
def clone(head: "Node | None") -> "Node | None":
    node = head
    while node is not None:              # 1. put each copy right after its original
        node.next = Node(node.val, node.next)
        node = node.next.next
    node = head
    while node is not None:              # 2. the copy of node.jump sits right after it
        if node.jump is not None:
            node.next.jump = node.jump.next
        node = node.next.next
    dummy = tail = Node()
    node = head
    while node is not None:              # 3. unzip: restore the original, chain the copies
        tail.next = node.next
        tail = tail.next
        node.next = tail.next
        node = node.next
    return dummy.next


# --- provided: do not edit ---
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None, jump=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        self.jump = jump


def run_clone(values: list[int], jumps: list[int | None]) -> list[list]:
    nodes = [Node(v) for v in values]
    for node, nxt in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        node.next = nxt
    for node, j in zip(nodes, jumps):
        node.jump = None if j is None else nodes[j]
    before = [(n.val, n.next, n.jump) for n in nodes]
    node = clone(nodes[0] if nodes else None)
    if any(n.val != v or n.next is not nx or n.jump is not j for n, (v, nx, j) in zip(nodes, before)):
        raise ValueError("the original list was changed: leave it (or restore it) as it was")
    originals, copies = {id(n) for n in nodes}, []
    while node is not None:
        if id(node) in originals:
            raise ValueError("the copy reuses original nodes: create new ones")
        if len(copies) == len(nodes):
            raise ValueError("the copy has more nodes than the original: is there a cycle?")
        copies.append(node)
        node = node.next
    where = {id(n): i for i, n in enumerate(copies)}
    if any(n.jump is not None and id(n.jump) not in where for n in copies):
        raise ValueError("a jump in the copy points outside the copy")
    return [[n.val for n in copies], [None if n.jump is None else where[id(n.jump)] for n in copies]]

explain.en: A `jump` can point at a node whose copy does not exist yet, so copy first and wire afterwards. A map from original to copy does it in O(n) time and memory. Interleaving needs O(1) extra: with each copy right after its original, `node.jump.next` is the copy of the jump target, so one pass wires every jump and a last pass unzips the lists, restoring the original. Traps: keying the map by value breaks with repeats, and finding each target by walking from the head is O(n²).
explain.es: Un `jump` puede apuntar a un nodo cuya copia todavía no existe, así que primero copia y después conecta. Un map de original a copia lo resuelve en O(n) de tiempo y memoria. Intercalar necesita O(1) extra: con cada copia justo después de su original, `node.jump.next` es la copia del destino del salto, así que una pasada conecta cada salto y una última separa las listas, restaurando el original. Trampas: usar el valor como clave falla con repetidos, y buscar cada destino caminando desde la cabeza es O(n²).
